thread:
sam (docs): Quick spotcheck: the /v1/rerank reference response example uses `top_documents` with full objects, but our runtime returns `document_indices` (ints) and a separate `documents` input. This mismatch broke one partner integration. Opening a tiny docs PR to correct shapes and add a migration note: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4012

lara (eng): Thanks — yeah the canonical response is `results: [{ query_index: number, document_indices: number[], scores: number[] }]`. We used a richer example on the page to be friendly, but that was inaccurate.

noah (sdk): Ouch. Our SDK samples currently deserialize `top_documents` when the docs page had that example, so SDKs that assumed object-based responses are wrong. I'll update the snippet and add a deserialization guide for partners who stored full doc objects.

jordan (api): Confirming: we intentionally separate the `documents` payload from `results` indices for bandwidth reasons. Please add a clear example showing how to map indices back to documents on the client side. Also add a note about stable ordering: `document_indices` are ranked by relevance (highest first).

sam (docs): Proposed corrected example that maps indices back to docs (will paste in PR):

```json
// request (abridged)
{
  "model": "rerank-large-v1",
  "queries": [{ "query": "tokenization docs", "top_k": 3 }],
  "documents": ["Doc A text", "Doc B text", "Doc C text"]
}
```

and response example:

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "query_index": 0,
      "document_indices": [0,2,1],
      "scores": [0.97, 0.65, 0.44]
    }
  ]
}
```

sam (docs): Then an inline JS snippet to map indices back to docs: `const ranked = results[0].document_indices.map(i => documents[i])` — will include that in the migration note.

lara (eng): Please also add a short table row under the response schema clarifying types: `document_indices: integer[] (indices into the documents array from the request)` and `scores: number[] (same length, aligned by index)`.

noah (sdk): I'll update the JS/TS snippet in the SDK with example mapping + a warning: "If you previously relied on an example that returned full document objects in the response, update to using indices and map them against your submitted documents." I'll reference docs PR 4012 from SDK PR.

jordan (api): Can we add a tiny example showing `documents` as objects with `id` so clients can persist stable ids: `documents: [{id: "d1", text: "..."}]` and then return `document_indices` that map to those objects? That helps teams who stored metadata server-side.

sam (docs): Good idea — adding both `documents` as strings and as `{id,text}` objects and an example mapping both to the response in the PR.

noah (sdk): SDK PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/802 — updating snippets, types, and adding a migration note in changelog.

deploy-bot: docs build passing for PR 4012 -> https://ci.redwood.ai/4012/builds/14

lara (eng): Tiny nit: in the mapping snippet show handling of multiple queries (i.e., iterate results by `query_index`) so users don't assume single-query only.

sam (docs): Added a compact multi-query mapping example and a short callout: "results array corresponds to the `queries` array; use `query_index` to correlate entries." Pushing final patch now.

jordan (api): Thanks everyone — after the SDK PR merges I'll ping partners who hit the break. Closing loop. :white_check_mark:
